title: Habits Take About 59 Days, Not 21
safety: General wellness only. The trial studied one everyday nutrition behaviour, so the timing is a reference point rather than a rule for every habit.

beats.headline: 59 days, not three weeks
beats.body: In a 2021 trial, the people who did form a habit reached peak automatic feeling after a median of 59 days. The popular three week rule wasn't a research finding.

beats.headline: What automatic actually means
beats.body: Automaticity is just how little thought a behaviour takes. It's the moment you do the thing before you decide to. That feeling builds slowly, and slowly is normal.

beats.headline: Pick the cue you'll repeat
beats.body: The trial compared anchoring the behaviour to a daily routine against anchoring it to a clock time. Neither worked better. So you could pick whichever one sticks.

beats.headline: Count repeats, not days
beats.body: Repeating the plan was the key predictor in this trial. A good place to start is a simple tally of times done, rather than watching the calendar.

beats.headline: Give it about two months
beats.body: The median of 59 days sits close to two months. If yours takes longer, that says nothing about you. Habit timing varied widely across the people studied.

beats.headline: Same spot, same stone
beats.body: Each repeat lands in the same place until the step needs no thought. You could start with the next one.
